# Crawler files (web)

<!-- module-flows:start (generated by .claude/bin/module-index; do not edit) -->

Flows: [`public-site`](../../flows/public-site/FLOW.md).

<!-- module-flows:end -->

## Purpose

Builds `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` for the public site ([public-site flow](../../flows/public-site/FLOW.md), PS-4). Crawlers read them; `app/robots.ts` and `app/sitemap.ts` only bind the default export to `readRobots` / `readSitemap`. Only the `production` stack is indexable; every other `APP_ENV` disallows the whole site.

## Techniques

Next.js metadata routes, built per request: `connection()` is awaited first, so the files are never prerendered and read the runtime `getServerEnv()` (`appEnv`, `webOrigin`). The metadata route sends `max-age=0`, so `next.config.ts` `headers()` has one entry per `CRAWLER_FILE_PATHS` value that sets `CRAWLER_FILES_CACHE_CONTROL` (`public, max-age=3600`) and wins over it. `proxy.ts` skips the two exact paths in its matcher, so they carry no nonce CSP (D17, PS-4). No cms-api call, no mock, no `index.ts`.

## Technologies

Next.js (`MetadataRoute`, `connection`), `server-only`.

## Entry points

`GET /robots.txt`, `GET /sitemap.xml`; `readRobots`, `readSitemap`, `buildRobots`, `buildSitemap`.

## Where to change what

- A new public page: add its path to `SITEMAP_PAGE_PATHS` (`configs/Api.endpoints.ts`); public pages only.
- A new rule (another disallowed prefix): the named constants in `CrawlerFiles.server.ts`.
- A new crawler file: one `CRAWLER_FILE_PATHS` entry, its route file in `app/`, and the proxy matcher entry; the `headers()` entry follows from the map.
- `CRAWLER_FILE_PATHS` and `CRAWLER_FILES_CACHE_CONTROL` live in files `next.config.ts` loads, so they keep no `@/` import.
